descripcion: The present simple describes habits and routines; the present continuous describes what is happening right now, at this moment. At A2 the goal is to choose the right one consistently and to recognise the signal words for each.

filas: I always work in the morning.

ejemplos.texto: I work every day from nine to five.
I'm working on a project right now.
She always drinks coffee in the morning.

notas: The present continuous is formed with am/is/are + -ing.
Words like always, usually, every day go with the present simple.
Words like now, right now, at the moment go with the present continuous.

contraste.es: Spanish has both forms (trabajo, estoy trabajando), but uses the simple present more often for things happening now. Spanish speakers therefore need to pay attention to marking the difference in English, where the continuous is required for right now.
contraste.de: German has only one present form (Ich arbeite means I work and I'm working). German speakers therefore often use the present simple for things happening now (Look, it rains) and need to practise the continuous for right now; the German word gerade is a good signal for it.
contraste.it: Italian has a continuous form (sto lavorando – I'm working), but uses the simple present much more often for things happening now. Italian speakers therefore tend to ask What do you do? when they mean What are you doing?
contraste.fr: French has only one simple present (je travaille means I work and I'm working); être en train de exists but is used much less than the English continuous. French speakers therefore often use the simple present for things happening now: Look, it rains.
contraste.pt: Portuguese uses a continuous form very often (estou a trabalhar in Portugal, estou trabalhando in Brazil), so the present continuous is familiar. Brazilian Portuguese also uses it with verbs like gostar (estou gostando), which leads to I'm liking it, where English uses I like it.

errores: Using the present simple for something happening right now.

traducciones.fr: Je suis en train de… en ce moment.

traducciones.de: Im Moment bin ich gerade am…
traducciones.fr: En ce moment, je suis en train de…

autochequeo: Is the present simple used for habits?
Is the present continuous used for now?
Is am/is/are present before every -ing form?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on the choice between present simple and present continuous. Check the form of the continuous carefully. Do not rewrite the text. Flag any mixed-up choice.
